_comment: Which delivered frames become which game clip. Run with:
python tools/fox_import.py --manifest tools/fox_clips.json
EVERY clip the game uses is generated from here, so assets/fox/animations/v2/ is
output, not source. The delivery in src_root is the source and is never modified.
src_root is where the artist's delivery was unpacked -- the only machine-specific
line in this file.
'start'/'end' index the source folder's frames sorted by their trailing number (so
'Fox Play 9' before 'Fox Play 10'), from 0, excluding 'end'. Omit them for the whole clip.
'scale' below 1 shrinks (smooth resample, then snapped back to the palette); 1.5 grows
(nearest, bit-exact). See the header of fox_import.py for why those two and no others.
'flip' mirrors a clip that was drawn facing right; the whole set must face left.
'isolate' keeps only the largest connected shape, which drops the grey ball the artist's
fox layer carries -- but only in frames where the fox is not touching it.
'stabilise' (shrinking only) swaps the smooth resample for one that doesn't shimmer:
one-frame blips are removed at full size, each output pixel takes the commonest colour
under it, and leftover specks are cleaned. 'loops' tells it the last frame is next to
the first. 'planted' warns if the fox's lowest pixels wander, i.e. it slides.
'palette_map' folds stray source colours onto palette ones, e.g. a shade the
colour-options shader can't recolour.
'src_in_repo' resolves 'src' against the repo root instead of src_root.
'hand_finished' means the artist has cleaned up the game frames themselves: the import
never overwrites them, it checks them (canvas, palette, hard edges, feet) instead.
--regenerate forces a rebuild and throws her cleanup away.
stalk, pounce and play are cut out of ONE delivered animation, 'Fox Play 02', which
contains a standing fox, a creep, a leap and a roll. They are placeholders in timing,
not in size: being slices of a continuous performance, none of them close into a loop.
(idle used to be cut from it too, until a proper one was drawn.)

clips.name: walk
clips._note: The best clip in the set: a clean 12-frame cycle whose ends meet. The size reference everything else is matched to, so its scale is 1.0 and must stay there.
cleanup: Nothing to do. This is the clip everything else was sized to match.
It's also the best loop in the set -- a good reference for the others.

clips.name: sleep
clips._note: Curled and breathing, ends meet. Same tier as walk, so no resize.
cleanup: Nothing to do. Loops correctly, reads lovely.

clips.name: sit
clips._note: Seated idle (not a sitting-down transition -- the fox is already seated in frame 1). Drawn two-thirds the size of walk, so x1.5 brings its 2px outline to walk's 3px exactly. Nearest-neighbour, so this is lossless and needs no cleanup.
cleanup: Scaled up 1.5x from what you sent, which made its outlines 3px like walk's.
The scaling was exact, so there shouldn't be anything to fix -- but worth a glance.
The game plays this one forwards then backwards, so the ends don't need to meet.

clips.name: run
clips._note: Same two-thirds tier as sit, same x1.5. Its cycle does not close -- that is an animation fix, not a size one, and is the reason it is not wired to anything.
cleanup: Scaled up 1.5x, same as sit. The size is fine now.

THE CYCLE DOESN'T CLOSE: going from the last frame back to the first is about a 1.5x bigger jump than the steps between the other frames, so it visibly hitches once per cycle. This is the one real animation fix in the set -- it's the last few frames needing to lead back into frame 1. Until then the game can't use this clip.

clips.name: idle
clips._note: The standing idle drawn for the purpose (Idle V2, delivered 2026-10-08): head tilt, a blink, a tail swish. Replaces the slice of Fox Play 02 that stood in for it. Sourced from the full-size 'Big' export, not her hand-resized 'Small' one: shrinking here measured 2-4x less twitch in the eyes and ears and keeps the feet still, where Small slid them about 1.5px. 'stabilise' because the full-size source boils (fur pixels flip for one frame and back), which reads as static once shrunk. The light orange #ea9c74 speckled through the fur is not one the colour-options shader knows, so it is folded into the main body orange. Scale matches her Small export, which matches walk. The source sits in the repo because that is where she pushed it; the .gdignore beside it keeps Godot from importing 23 full-HD frames into the build.
clips._loops_note: false while the game ping-pongs it (the tail doesn't close yet). Set true once the artist adds the bridge frames and fox_v2.gd plays it as a LOOP.
clips._hand_finished_note: Handed to the artist 2026-10-08 to clean up the game frames directly. From here the frames in 'out' are the clip and the import only checks them; --regenerate would overwrite her work.
cleanup: Your new idle -- the head tilt, the blink and the tail. Shrunk from the full-size frames you sent (the 'Big' folder) rather than your resized ones.

THE TAIL DOESN'T QUITE CLOSE THE LOOP: from the last frame back to the first, the tail jumps from low and swept right back up, about twice a normal step. One or two in-between tail frames after frame 23 would let it loop. Until then the game plays it forwards then backwards.

The pale orange (#ea9c74) in the fur has been changed to the main orange, because the fox colour options can't recolour it. If you want a highlight shade, tell us and we'll teach the colour options about it.

clips.name: stalk
clips._note: Low creeping walk. Starts after the fox has left the ball behind, so the ball is a separate shape and 'isolate' drops it. Thinned to every second frame: the creep is slow and 40 frames of it is more than the motion carries. Faces right in the source, so it is flipped.
cleanup: The low creep. Every 2nd frame was kept -- the original was slower than it needed.

Doesn't loop, and unlike the others it can't be played backwards to hide that (a walk in reverse is a moonwalk), so the game isn't using this one yet. Low priority -- it's a bonus clip, not one the game needs.

clips.name: pounce
clips._note: The leap: gather, extend, front paws reach. Stops at the last frame before the paws touch the ball -- both so the game's own ball provides the impact, and because once the fox touches it the ball stops being a separate shape and 'isolate' can no longer drop it. Faces right in the source, so it is flipped.
cleanup: The leap. Stops deliberately on the frame before the paws touch the ball, so the game can put its own ball under them.

Plays once rather than looping, so the ends don't need to meet. What would help is the last frame sitting comfortably next to the first frame of the standing idle, since that's what plays straight after it.

clips.name: play
clips._note: On its back, kicking the ball. Loops on its own. NOTE the fox is holding the ball throughout, and the delivered Fox layer draws a grey ball of its own, so that ball is baked into these frames -- it cannot be isolated out the way the other clips can, because the fox is touching it. Fine as a placeholder, wrong next to the game's blue ball.
cleanup: On its back, kicking the ball.

THE BALL IS DRAWN INTO THESE FRAMES. On the other clips the grey ball could be removed automatically, but here the fox is holding it so it can't be separated. The game draws its own blue ball, so the grey one will clash with it.

If this section could be redrawn with the paws in the same places but NO ball in the fox layer at all -- ball only on the ball layer, like you already do -- the game can put its own ball into the fox's paws.
